title: 2008 AMC 12A Problem 5
statement: Suppose that \[\dfrac{2x}{3} - \dfrac{x}{6}\] is an integer. Which of the following statements must be true about \(x?\)

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
It is even, but not necessarily a multiple of
\(3.\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: It is a multiple of \(3,\) but not necessarily even.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
It is a multiple of \(6,\) but not necessarily a multiple of
\(12.\)

solutions.text:
Combining the fractions, \[ \dfrac{2x}{3} - \dfrac{x}{6} = \dfrac{4x - x}{6} = \dfrac{x}{2}. \]

This is an integer exactly when \(x\) is even. The example \(x = 4\) is even but not a multiple of \(3,\) which rules out every other statement.

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Combine the two fractions over a common denominator
Simplify to \(\dfrac{x}{2},\) then decide what divisibility condition makes this an integer
